hints.title: Match the inputs to f
hints.body: For f(x+2), find the x-values for which its input is 2 and 4. Sketch how this moves the original area.
hints.recap: Changing f(x) to f(x+a) shifts its graph horizontally.
hints.pitfall: The limits refer to x; the input fed into f is x+2.
hints.pause: Choose the limits that cover the same part of the original graph.

recall.reminder: Changing f(x) to f(x+a) shifts its graph horizontally.

hints.title: Account for the added height
hints.body: The extra +1 raises the graph by one unit across your new interval. Work out the area of that added rectangle.
hints.recap: A constant added inside an integral contributes its height times the interval width.
hints.pitfall: Adding 1 to the function does not always add 1 to the integral.
hints.pause: Combine the unchanged area with your rectangle area.

recall.reminder: A constant vertical shift adds its height times the interval width to the signed area.

solution:
With u=x+2, the limits x=0 and x=2 become u=2 and u=4. Hence ∫02f(x+2)dx = ∫24f(u)du =A.

Therefore ∫02[f(x+2)+1]dx =A+∫021dx =A+2.

Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Shift integral limits and add the area from a vertical translation
